deliberateDuplication: The FFI is three files in lockstep: the Rust #[no_mangle] export, its entry in the hand-maintained core/include/reelcut_core.h, and its wrapper in app/Sources/ReelCore.swift. Each export is deliberately stated three times. (source: CLAUDE.md)

The op table is mirrored on purpose. core/src/edit.rs holds the semantics and core/src/op_table.rs the arguments. ReelOps.swift's typed builders, AgentCatalog*.swift's tools and spec §6 mirror them: change one, change all four. (source: CLAUDE.md)

Agent parity: every user-visible edit gets an MCP mirror, meaning an AgentServer+<Feature>.swift handler, a catalog entry and a comment naming the UI path it mirrors. UI command code and agent handlers intentionally parallel each other. (source: app/CLAUDE.md)

Swift mirrors of core types are kept on purpose: ReelOpSchema.swift mirrors op_schema.rs; ReelEdit.swift mirrors outcome.rs; ProjectSnapshot/TextProps/MotionProps/WordProps and ProjectSnapshot+Graphic mirror the spec §5.2 model (model_words.rs, model_graphic.rs); ReelOps.documentLevelNames mirrors scope.rs's refused_inside. (source: app/CLAUDE.md)

core/src/model_graphic.rs's check_schema COPIES the graphic engine's sentences, because no model module may name the graphic crate (G-2). It duplicates graphic/src/props.rs on purpose. (source: core/CLAUDE.md)
core/src/agent.rs is a generic MCP server copied from Rasterize; do not add domain knowledge. (source: core/CLAUDE.md)

Theme.swift, Controls.swift, OptionControls.swift, Sheets.swift, EditorChrome.swift and FileDropView.swift are copied from Rasterize and kept in sync rather than forked. The divergences are recorded: StickerButton's pill (SH-1) and BlockSliderCell.drawBar (SH-2). (source: app/CLAUDE.md)
MotionProps.dictionary and WordStyle.dictionary both write every key, with NSNull for nil slots, because the core deep-merges. This is the same rule stated twice on purpose. (source: app/CLAUDE.md)
agent/src is meant to be byte-identical to ~/devel/rasterize/agent/src/, with one diff applied to both. (source: CLAUDE.md)

The price function is answered by both agent/src/pricing.ts and tools/proof/prices.py against agent/prices/cases.json. Both reducers (update.py, priceTable.ts) answer reduce_cases.json. (source: CLAUDE.md)
silence2_proof.py spells the reversed mirror in Python on purpose, because a reference walk must not import what it checks. (source: tools/proof/README.md)

notes: agent/ (TypeScript, which the scan does not support) is not under any root. Its intended byte-identity with Rasterize's agent/src is recorded as a rule for context only.

tools/ stays ignored whole. Its Swift probes and harness compile app/Sources, and its Python proofs deliberately re-derive core arithmetic as independent oracles, so duplicates found there are not consolidation candidates.
core/target, graphic/target, tools/proof/graphics_spike/target and tools/proof/tools are git-ignored build output or tooling and sit outside every root, so no ignore entry is needed.
archive/ holds only non-source markdown (20 files, 0 source lines) and is historical per CLAUDE.md. It is outside the roots.
Most shared-looking Swift/Rust pairs, such as model mirrors and op builders, are deliberate mirrors that the startup parity check enforces. Treat them as lockstep, not as consolidation targets.
Rasterize-copied chrome files (Theme, Controls, OptionControls, Sheets, EditorChrome, FileDropView) should not be forked or merged locally.
